task:
Create a NetworkPolicy named 'np-backend' in namespace 'project-snake'.

Setup — create the namespace and pods first:
  kubectl create ns project-snake
  kubectl run backend-app --image=nginx:1.21 -n project-snake --labels=app=backend
  kubectl run db1-app    --image=nginx:1.21 -n project-snake --labels=app=db1
  kubectl run db2-app    --image=nginx:1.21 -n project-snake --labels=app=db2
  kubectl run vault-app  --image=nginx:1.21 -n project-snake --labels=app=vault

NetworkPolicy requirements for 'np-backend':
  - Applies to Pods with label: app=backend
  - Policy type: Egress
  - Allow egress ONLY to:
      * Pods with label app=db1  on port 1111
      * Pods with label app=db2  on port 2222
  - All other egress from backend pods is DENIED
    (connections to vault-app on port 3333 must be blocked)

Verify:
  kubectl describe networkpolicy np-backend -n project-snake

Expected: Two egress rules — one for db1:1111 and one for db2:2222.
detailed_hints: A NetworkPolicy with policyTypes: [Egress] and explicit egress rules implicitly denies all other egress
If you also need DNS: add egress rule for port 53 UDP/TCP to kube-dns pods or use namespaceSelector for kube-system
YAML structure: spec.egress is a list; each item has 'to' (podSelector) and 'ports' (port number)

validators.command: kubectl get networkpolicy np-backend -n project-snake -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'
kubectl get networkpolicy np-backend -n project-snake -o jsonpath='{.spec.policyTypes[0]}'
kubectl get networkpolicy np-backend -n project-snake -o jsonpath='{.spec.egress}' | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(len(json.load(sys.stdin)))"
